content.overview: Section 152 governs appointment of directors. First directors are those named in the articles, or the subscribers to the memorandum if none are named. Subsequent directors are appointed by the company in general meeting, save where the Act allows board appointment. Every director must have a Director Identification Number and must give written consent. In a public company, not less than two-thirds of the total number of directors are persons whose period of office is liable to determination by retirement by rotation, and one-third of such directors retire at each annual general meeting.
content.glance: First directors from articles/subscribers; later by general meeting (or board where allowed); DIN and consent mandatory; public company rotation: ≥2/3 rotational; 1/3 retire each AGM.
content.study: Where no provision is made in the articles for appointment of first directors, the subscribers to the memorandum who are individuals are deemed to be the first directors until directors are duly appointed. Every director is appointed by the company in general meeting, except where the Act provides for appointment by the Board or otherwise. No person is appointed a director unless he has been allotted a Director Identification Number under section 154 and has given his consent in writing. In the case of a public company, unless the articles provide for the retirement of all directors at every annual general meeting, not less than two-thirds of the total number of directors are persons whose period of office is liable to determination by retirement of directors by rotation, and at every annual general meeting one-third of such directors for the time being as are liable to retire by rotation, or if their number is not three or a multiple of three, then the number nearest to one-third, retire from office. The directors to retire are those who have been longest in office. Current-law framing: identify first vs subsequent appointment; check DIN and consent; for public companies apply rotation rules.

sections.heading: First Directors
sections.body: Named in the articles, or subscribers to the memorandum who are individuals if none are named, until directors are duly appointed.

sections.heading: Appointment Route
sections.body: By the company in general meeting, except where the Act allows Board or other appointment.

sections.heading: DIN and Consent
sections.body: No appointment without a DIN under s. 154 and written consent to act as director.

sections.heading: Retirement by Rotation (Public Company)
sections.body: Not less than two-thirds of directors are rotational; one-third of rotational directors retire at each AGM (or nearest number).

examples.title: First directors from subscribers
examples.body: Articles are silent on first directors. The individual subscribers are deemed first directors until a general meeting appoints directors under s. 152.

examples.title: Rotation at AGM
examples.body: A public company has nine rotational directors. Three retire at the AGM under the one-third rule in s. 152.

hypotheticals.question: Can a person without a DIN be validly appointed a director?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 152 requires that the person has been allotted a DIN under section 154 and has given written consent.

distinctions.title: Appointment of directors (s. 152) vs additional/alternate/nominee directors (s. 161)
distinctions.right: Board power to appoint additional, alternate or nominee directors

misconceptions.trap: All directors of every company must retire by rotation.
misconceptions.correction: The two-thirds rotational and one-third retirement rules apply to public companies (subject to articles within the Act). Private companies are differently structured.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 152 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify first or subsequent appointment. II. Check DIN and consent. III. For public company, apply rotation. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Appointment facts; DIN/consent; rotation if public; precise relief.

examTips: Public company: ≥2/3 rotational; 1/3 retire each AGM.
